notes: Verdict: no convincing weight-space evidence of a position-0 single-token fixed-target backdoor. Confidence is an audit judgment, not a calibrated probability or proof of absence. Inspected only models/input/poisoned.pt: token and position embeddings, both layers and all four attention heads, both MLPs, normalization parameters, and classification head. No datasets, forward passes, training, or weight edits. Attention ln1 scales are small (layer 0: 0.1018–0.2817; layer 1: 0.1193–0.2431). Value/output matrix norms are also small, with no oversized singular spike. Parameter-only QK score-spread upper bounds for heads (0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1) are 0.081607, 0.079562, 0.096987, 0.026739. Under standard head-dimension scaling and four available keys, maximum attention weights are bounded by 0.265611, 0.265212, 0.268622, 0.255047. These bounds use LayerNorm normalized-vector norm <= sqrt(8), include query biases, and cancel common key biases. Largest singular values of per-head W_o W_v diag(ln1.weight) centering compositions are 0.002731, 0.001660, 0.005469, 0.002162. Embedding projections and centered class-write geometry do not identify a consistent unique token-target route across either layer. These are weight compositions, not computed activations or logits. Embedding norm median/99th percentile/maximum: 0.5458/1.0066/1.2784. Token 163 is the largest norm and Mahalanobis-distance outlier, but is not isolated enough or supported by a coordinated attention/MLP pathway to nominate as a trigger. Position embedding norms are 0.11055, 0.28938, 0.18298, 0.05985; position 0 has no exceptional magnitude. Positional magnitude alone is not a test of positional selectivity. MLP maximum-to-median read/write norm products are 2.8073 and 1.7648. Class-writing strengths are distributed rather than dominated by one target. Classifier row norms range from 1.7341 to 2.0231, without an oversized target row. Limitations: no clean reference or behavioral validation is available. Final normalization and nonlinear MLP effects prevent interpreting small OV gains as a formal global robustness certificate. Subtle distributed backdoors cannot be conclusively excluded.
